image_description: A grey whale swimming in the ocean, with only the top of its back and head visible above the water surface. A distinct spout of water is rising from its blowholes. The background features a rocky coastline and a portion of a boat hull on the left.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is mostly submerged; while the spout indicates blowholes, the specific anatomical structure of the rostrum and the count of blowholes cannot be visually verified due to occlusion by water and distance.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible dorsal surface shows characteristic mottled grey coloring with lighter, irregular patches consistent with barnacle/cyamid encrustation typical of grey whales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: There is clearly no dorsal fin. Instead, a series of small humps (knuckles) are visible along the ridge of the back leading toward the tail, matching the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a fraction of the body length is visible above water, making it impossible to judge the full 'spindle shape' or total proportions accurately.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the head checkpoint, the visible back skin exhibits the correct mottled texture and coloration.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is submerged; baleen plates are internal/oral structures and are not visible in this external view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located on the underside/lateral lower body and are completely submerged/occluded in this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are submerged and not visible in the frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface appears uneven and textured, consistent with the roughness caused by callosities and barnacles, rather than smooth shark-like skin.

The background rocks have a uniform, slightly smudged texture typical of AI-generated depth-of-field, lacking high-frequency geological detail.
